My dear book buddy Clovis, as an Aniimo researcher myself, I feel obliged to remind you that keeping a Budclaw is not an easy thing to do... Actually, it’s not easy to keep any Aniimo.

First of all, there’s something you need to know about Budclaws.
1. Heartblooms
Heartblooms, the small buds on top of each Budclaw’s head, are parasitic entities present from birth. They provide nutrients for their host through photosynthesis. That’s why Budclaws are diurnal and enjoy sunbathing so much—it keeps them healthy.

2. Lifetime Partners
Budclaws are highly faithful Aniimo—they have only one partner for life.
The heartblooms on their heads (those small buds) reflect how close they are to their mates.
That means if you ever find a flower on your Budclaw buddy’s head, congratulations! You’ll soon have a couple of Budclaws and probably many baby Budclaws in the future.
Also, if a Budclaw has a flower on its head, other would-be mates will instinctively keep their distance.

Second, you must interact with your Budclaw buddy in the correct way.
- You should never maltreat it (which I believe you’d never do).
- Make sure you’re there for it and comfort it when it feels down (they are usually not that hard to cheer up).
- If a Budclaw ever buries itself deep into the soil, that’s a serious sign—it could be depressed, and you must intervene immediately.
